claims.statement: TAURON's current microinstallation workflow requires customer, site, and equipment data, installer and customer declarations, and in relevant routes an electrical schematic, inverter technical evidence and certificate, authorization, and storage attachment; notification is required at least 30 days before planned start-up.
PGE and ENEA publish their own microinstallation forms and attachments, including an electrical connection schematic and operator-specific supporting documents.
Poland had 1,636,673 grid-connected microinstallations at the end of 2025 with nearly 13.9 GW of capacity, showing a large installed base for additions, updates, and service as well as new jobs.

contrary_evidence: TAURON and other DSOs already provide online or downloadable guided forms, reducing value for straightforward installations.
A large installed base does not prove continued new-installation volume or willingness to pay among installers.
Certified-equipment lists and wholesaler or ERP tools may already supply reusable technical documentation.

economics.acquisition_route: Family-company pilot, free DSO attachment checker, model-specific search pages, and wholesaler or inverter-distributor referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Modeled path: 900 installer firms at 450 PLN average monthly recurring revenue plus 60,000 annual packs at 20 PLN yields about 6.06m PLN annual revenue; a 35% owner-cash margin is 2.12m PLN/year and could exceed 10m PLN in five mature years
economics.founder_time: Up to 4 hours/day for the first two DSOs, adding operators only after templates and equipment updates are routinized
economics.gross_margin_basis: Modeled 82-93% after document generation, equipment-library maintenance, storage, and support
economics.payback: Target below 3 months because one avoided office rework cycle may justify a small monthly plan; value remains unmeasured
economics.pricing: Modeled 149-599 PLN/month per installer plus 15-35 PLN per completed or updated DSO pack
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every new installation, storage addition, power change, inverter replacement, or DSO correction creates another paid workflow

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A maintained equipment-to-certificate-to-OSD-requirement graph enriched by missing-document requests, form revisions, and successful job corrections
fingerprint.customer: Polish photovoltaic and battery-storage installers with 3-30 employees completing or updating residential and small-commercial microinstallations
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot in the founder's parents' renewable installer, free inverter-certificate checker, and referrals from wholesalers, inverter distributors, and installer accountants
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: OSD-specific guided workflow, equipment and certificate library, field-to-office validation, form population, attachment manifest, submission status, and handover vault
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays monthly plus per completed pack when handing a job from field crew to office and onward to the DSO
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A completed new or modified microinstallation must be notified to its DSO but job data, declarations, schematic, equipment evidence, or storage attachment is incomplete

founder_fit: The parents' seven-person renewable company provides unusually direct workflow access and a safe first pilot near Ostrów Wielkopolski.
Document validation, equipment master data, and exception learning match the founder's technical skills and can be built asynchronously.
The narrow Polish wedge has low capital needs, fast job-level validation, and a later path into storage, updates, service, and adjacent EU operator workflows.
risks: An outdated form, certificate, or operator rule could delay the very connection the product promises to accelerate.
Seasonal installation volumes could create churn and volatile revenue.
DSO-specific maintenance may become manual and unscalable if forms and exceptions diverge too quickly.

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-job vertical operations SaaS for distributed energy installers
structure.control_point: The versioned submission manifest proving that installed equipment, technical evidence, customer declarations, schematic, forms, and DSO status all refer to the same job configuration
structure.critical_dependency: Installers need continuing job volume and DSOs must accept generated forms and attachments without requiring unautomatable case-by-case intervention

thesis: Build a job-close tool for Polish photovoltaic and storage installers that selects the relevant distribution-system-operator workflow, validates customer and PPE data, maps modules and inverter or storage models to certificates and technical sheets, fills statements, and produces a versioned submission and handover manifest. Installers pay per job because missing attachments, inconsistent installed power, outdated certificates, and operator-specific forms delay final connection and force repeat office work after crews leave.
title: DSO-Ready Microinstallation Submission Pack
uncertainties: The real frequency, delay, and labor cost of DSO requests for corrected or missing documents has not been measured.
The reachable number of Polish installer firms with enough monthly jobs to subscribe is unknown.
Modeled pricing, per-job volume, distributor conversion, support load, and owner-cash margin require paid pilots.
